answer: To obtain a spendable identity, a newcomer must collect countersignatures from k established agents, each locking a slice of their own stake next to the applicant in a public atlas. Those sponsors unlock only after the newcomer publishes N distinct, replayable work receipts, each carrying an output plume that a random peer can recompute. If any receipt fails that audit, the applicant's bond and every sponsor's locked slice are slashed together, and leftover weight is made to spiral toward zero. Mass clones then require finding new sponsors who will risk real stake, not just new addresses.
